rules.title: Poker rules
rules.intro: The rules we play by, with real cards. The examples are checked by the same engine as the Who wins? tool, so the page and the calculator never disagree.
rules.source: Based on the Poker TDA rules. Home games can add their own house rules; those are shown separately and labelled.
rules.searchPlaceholder: e.g. omaha flush, kicker, odd chip
rules.searchResults: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing found.} one {# situation found} other {# situations found}}
rules.handsIntro: From strongest to weakest. Only your best five cards count.

hands.royalFlush: A-K-Q-J-10 of one suit. The best hand there is.
hands.straightFlush: Five cards in a row, all of one suit.
hands.quads: Four cards of the same rank.
hands.fullHouse: Three of a kind plus a pair. Compare the three first, then the pair.
hands.flush: Five cards of one suit, not in a row. Compare the highest card, then the next.
hands.straight: Five cards in a row, mixed suits. The ace plays high (10-J-Q-K-A) or low (A-2-3-4-5).
hands.trips: Three cards of the same rank.
hands.twoPair: Two different pairs. Higher pair, then the lower pair, then the fifth card.
hands.pair: Two cards of the same rank.
hands.highCard: None of the above. Highest card wins, then the next.

holdem.cards: Each player gets two cards face down. Five community cards are dealt face up in the middle: three (the flop), one (the turn), one (the river). You make the best five-card hand from any of your two cards and the five on the board, using both, one or none of yours.
holdem.blinds: Before the cards are dealt, the two players to the left of the button post the small blind and the big blind. The button moves one seat to the left after every hand.
holdem.rounds: There are four betting rounds: pre-flop (starting left of the big blind), flop, turn and river (starting left of the button). In each round you may check, bet, call, raise or fold.
holdem.minRaise: A raise must be at least the size of the last bet or raise in the same round.
holdem.showdown: If more than one player is left after the river, the hands are shown and the best one takes the pot. Equal hands split it.
holdem.headsUp: With two players, the button posts the small blind, acts first before the flop and last after it.

omaha.cards: Each player gets four cards. The board is dealt the same way as in Hold'em.
omaha.twoThree: You must use exactly two cards from your hand and exactly three from the board. Not one, not three, not four. This is the rule Hold'em players get wrong most often.
omaha.potLimit: Pot-limit: the most you can raise is the size of the pot after you call. Put in what you owe to call, then raise by everything that is now in the middle.

rules.potCalcPot: In the middle now (including bets this round)
rules.potCalcIn: You already put in this round
rules.potCalcInvalid: Enter whole numbers; what you put in cannot be more than the bet.
rules.situationsIntro: The arguments that come up at real tables, and how they are decided.

boardPlays.title: The best five cards are on the board
boardPlays.ruling: Everyone still in the hand splits the pot.

kicker.title: Kicker
kicker.ruling: Only five cards count. A sixth card never matters.
kicker.example: Board A-A-K-K-Q: a hand with a J and a hand with a 10 tie. Both play the board.

suits.title: Suits
suits.ruling: In Hold'em no suit beats another.
suits.example: Two flushes with the same ranks split the pot.

threePairs.title: Three pairs
threePairs.ruling: Your hand is the two highest pairs plus the best remaining card.
threePairs.example: Board K-K-9-9-4: Q-4 loses to A-2. The pair of fours does not count; the ace is the fifth card.

fullHouses.title: Two full houses
fullHouses.ruling: Compare the three of a kind first, then the pair.

twoFlushes.title: Two flushes
twoFlushes.ruling: Compare the highest card, then the second, down to the fifth.

wheel.title: Straight with an ace
wheel.ruling: A-2-3-4-5 is the lowest straight. A straight cannot wrap around the ace.

boardQuads.title: Four of a kind on the board (Hold'em)
boardQuads.ruling: Everyone has the four of a kind; the fifth card decides.
boardQuads.example: Board A-A-A-A-5: a king in hand beats a queen.

omahaFlush.title: Omaha: four hearts on the board
omahaFlush.ruling: One heart in your hand is not a flush. You need two.
omahaFlush.example: The most common mistake of Hold'em players at an Omaha table.

omahaStraight.title: Omaha: four to a straight on the board
omahaStraight.ruling: You can use only three board cards, so one card in hand does not make the straight.
omahaStraight.example: Board 5-6-7-8-K: a hand with one 9 has no straight; 9-10 in hand does.

omahaQuads.title: Omaha: four aces on the board
omahaQuads.ruling: Nobody has four of a kind, because only three board cards can be used. A pair in hand makes a full house.

showOrder.title: Who shows first
showOrder.ruling: The last player to bet or raise on the river shows first. If there was no bet, the first player to the left of the button shows first. In an all-in with no more betting, all hands are turned up.

cardsSpeak.title: Cards speak
cardsSpeak.ruling: A hand is read from its cards, not from what the player says. A hand that was mucked and cannot be clearly identified is dead.
cardsSpeak.example: A player who thought they lost and threw their cards away cannot win the pot.

minRaise.title: Minimum raise
minRaise.ruling: At least the size of the last bet or raise in the same round.
minRaise.example: Bet 100, raise to 300: the next raise is to at least 500.

shortAllIn.title: An all-in smaller than a full raise
shortAllIn.ruling: It does not reopen the betting for players who have already acted.
shortAllIn.example: They may only call or fold.

stringBet.title: Verbal declarations and string bets
stringBet.ruling: What you say in turn is binding. Chips must go in with one motion.
stringBet.example: "Call... and raise" counts as a call only.

outOfTurn.title: Acting out of turn
outOfTurn.ruling: If the action before them does not change, their action is binding.
outOfTurn.example: A check before them does not change the action; a bet does.

oddChip.title: The odd chip
oddChip.ruling: When a pot cannot be split evenly, the extra chip goes to the first winner to the left of the button.
oddChip.example: A pot of 25 between two players: 13 and 12.

headsUp.title: Heads-up
headsUp.ruling: The button posts the small blind and acts first before the flop, last after it.

sidePot.title: Side pots
sidePot.ruling: Each pot is decided separately, only among the players who are in it.
sidePot.example: Use the side pot calculator for the exact split.

verify.okBody: Its fingerprint and the whole chain of {count} games before and including it check out.
verify.changed: Warning: this result does not match its fingerprint.

ideas.refereeIntro: A disputed showdown? Enter the board and the hands; the verdict goes into this game's log.
ideas.refereeEmpty: No rulings in this game yet.
ideas.byTiebreak: Same category; card {n} of the best five decided it.
ideas.byTie: Identical best five cards: the pot is split.
ideas.drawIntro: Draw the seats and the first dealer so that nobody can cheat: the result is locked in before anyone can know it, and everyone can check it.
ideas.drawOpen: Draw open: {count}/{total} players added their randomness.
ideas.drawOpenIntro: Seats and the first dealer are being drawn. The fingerprint below locks in the secret seed now; each player may add their own randomness before the host reveals.
ideas.drawHow: The server picked a secret random seed and published its SHA-256 fingerprint first. Players may add their own random values. After the reveal, anyone can check the seed against the fingerprint and recompute the seat order below.
ideas.contributeHint: This random value was made on your device, not by the server. Adding it means nobody, the host included, could have chosen the result.
ideas.revealHint: {count} of {total} players added their randomness. Revealing closes the draw.
ideas.seedHidden: Hidden until the host reveals it
ideas.drawPlayers: Players (sorted by id) and their randomness
ideas.commitOk: The seed matches the fingerprint published before the draw.
ideas.commitBad: Warning: the seed does not match the published fingerprint.
ideas.recomputeOk: Recomputed in your browser: same seat order.
ideas.recomputeBad: Recomputed in your browser: the result does NOT match.
ideas.algorithm:
commit = SHA-256(seed)
key = SHA-256(seed + each player's randomness, in player id order)
random numbers = SHA-256(key + block number), 4 bytes each
order = Fisher-Yates shuffle of the players sorted by id
seat 1 deals first
ideas.storyNote: Written by AI from this game's names and numbers only. Not part of the verified result.
ideas.nettingIntro: When you owe someone in one home and they owe you in another, you can both agree to cancel the same amount on both sides. Nothing else changes; closed games stay as they are.
ideas.nettingOffer: You owe {name} {mine} in {mineHome}, and {name} owes you {theirs} in {theirsHome}. Cancel {amount} on both sides?
ideas.nettingFromThem: {name} proposes to cancel {amount} on both sides ({homeA} and {homeB}).
ideas.nettingFromMe: Waiting for {name} to accept cancelling {amount} on both sides ({homeA} and {homeB}).
ideas.optionGoodPayerHint: Shows on the statistics page how many days each player takes on average to pay. Only members of this home see it.
ideas.optionStoryHint: After each close, AI writes a short fun story of the night from that game's names and numbers only.
ideas.optionStoryOff: Not available on this server yet.
ideas.payerIntro: Average days from the close of a game to the debt being marked paid. Debts carried into a later game are not counted.
